response.sql: WITH groups AS (SELECT BillingState, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Invoice GROUP BY BillingState), stats AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt, SUM(cnt) AS total_cnt FROM groups), shares AS (SELECT g.cnt, g.cnt * 1.0 / s.total_cnt AS share, s.avg_cnt FROM groups g CROSS JOIN stats s) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_invoices, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(cnt - avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_count FROM shares WHERE cnt > avg_cnt;

assumptions.assumption: Invoices with no billing state are those where BillingState IS NULL; GROUP BY places all NULLs in one group. Empty-string states are kept as their own group, separate from NULL.
The average count per group is the mean of the group counts (one value per state group, including the NULL group), not the mean invoice count per invoice.
A group is kept only when its count is strictly greater than the average count.
The average excess is the mean of (group count minus average count) over the kept groups, and the shares are computed as count divided by the total of all group counts, using real-number division.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat blank or whitespace-only billing states as having no billing state, so they fall into the same group as NULL.
alternatives.sql: WITH groups AS (SELECT NULLIF(TRIM(BillingState), '') AS BillingState, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Invoice GROUP BY NULLIF(TRIM(BillingState), '')), stats AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt, SUM(cnt) AS total_cnt FROM groups), shares AS (SELECT g.cnt, g.cnt * 1.0 / s.total_cnt AS share, s.avg_cnt FROM groups g CROSS JOIN stats s) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_invoices, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(cnt - avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_count FROM shares WHERE cnt > avg_cnt;
